original.target_description: Study 3: US MTurk participants randomized to a lamb-chops advertisement with versus without a living lamb; two candidate between-condition tests, empathy and willingness to eat meat. The supplied locator does not distinguish the outcome/test.

n.sample_role: Study 3 participants; sample consistent with both reported t(185) tests
n.exclusions: No Study 3 exclusions reported in the participant/results sections.
n.quote: 187 US Americans were recruited through Amazon MTurk

es.quote: participants showed more empathy, t(185) = −3.51, p = 0.001; they were less willing to eat meat when the lamb was presented than when it was not presented, t(185) = 3.33, p = 0.001

p.quote: participants showed more empathy, t(185) = −3.51, p = 0.001; they were less willing to eat meat when the lamb was presented than when it was not presented, t(185) = 3.33, p = 0.001

replication.target_description: Study 1: animal–meat reminder versus meat-alone condition; empathy and willingness-to-eat scores averaged across lamb, cow, and pig images. Table 1 contains separate condition correlations for both outcomes. The supplied locator does not distinguish them.

n.sample_role: Retained Study 1 participants; missing variable data (0 to 0.7%) estimated with FIML
n.exclusions: From 353 recruited: duplicate IP addresses (n = 3), non-meat-eaters (n = 13), and failed attention checks (n = 38) excluded.
n.location: Accepted manuscript p. 9, Participants and procedure; p. 12, Results
n.quote: Duplicate IP addresses (n = 3), those who do not eat meat (n = 13), and participants who failed an attention check (n = 38) were excluded. This left 299 participants

es.location: Accepted manuscript p. 13, Table 1, column 1; the supplied p. 6 does not contain Study 1 results in this manuscript version
es.quote: 5. Animal empathy .43***; 8. Willingness to eat meat -.31***; *** p < .001

p.location: Accepted manuscript p. 13, Table 1, column 1; the supplied p. 6 does not contain Study 1 results in this manuscript version
p.quote: 5. Animal empathy .43***; 8. Willingness to eat meat -.31***; *** p < .001

reported_success.quote: Overall the animal-meat reminder (vs. meat alone) manipulation clearly induced animal empathy and meat distress and decreased meat consumption willingness (see Table 1).

notes: The assigned inputs for 1581 and 1582 are identical, including a combined empathy/willingness description and the same locators. No supplied information maps either ID to one outcome. To avoid inferring assignment from input order, es.value and p.value are null for both IDs; the candidate printed tests are retained in the field quotes. Original candidates: empathy t(185) = −3.51, p = 0.001; willingness t(185) = 3.33, p = 0.001 (p. 766). Replication candidates: condition–empathy r = .43, p < .001; condition–willingness r = -.31, p < .001 (accepted manuscript Table 1, p. 13, column 1; condition coded +1 animal-meat reminder, −1 control). No conversion performed. target_match remains unknown at the individual-effect level because outcome/test mapping is insufficient; the studies and manipulations match. Replication uses three animal/meat pairings rather than only the original lamb stimulus. Sources are full primary papers with titles verified against the supplied references. Original PDF extraction encodes minus signs as a control character and equals signs as ¼; quotes normalize those glyphs and whitespace. Replication quotes normalize whitespace. Reported success is the authors’ narrative verdict for the two named outcomes, not an inference from significance.
